newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen clamber off lows on JGB rebound.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen clamber off lows on JGB rebound.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures made a moderate recovery as talk of heavy cash bond buying by a major Japanese life insurance company lifted Japanese government bond (JGB) futures late on Tuesday, dealers said.

They said JGB futures came under pressure early in the day on fears U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, in a scheduled meeting with Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, would push for a supplementary budget to boost Japan's economy

But the long end of the curve rose sharply in afternoon trade, propelling Euroyen futures higher, when those fears failed to materialise and a six-year bond auction had a better than expected response.
"One of the big lifers started buying 164(th issue) JGBs on the cash market. They were supposed to have bought about 200 billion yen worth," said a trader with a European futures house.
March JGBs settled at 126.40 against their opening 126.26.
December Euroyen was quoted at 99.20 at 1112 GMT against its IMM close at 99.19 after hitting a low of 99.17.
"There's very strong consensus that there'll be no change in the Bank of Japan's monetary policy so there was fresh buying interest below 99.20," said a Japanese bank dealer.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly firmer in fairly thin trade as players began their vigil for the February non-farm payrolls report, due on Friday.
Interest was also hampered by caution ahead of the second part of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.

"Technically, the market looks very bearish but nobody wants to do anything ahead of Friday's numbers," said the trader at the European house. "The market is already pricing in no change in rates till the summer."
Dealers had mixed reactions to a halving of the minimum tick size for Eurodollar futures with some expecting it to boost trading volumes while others were less convinced.

"I think it'll work better on SIMEX than in Chicago because the trading ranges are a lot tighter here," said the trader at the European house, noting that the move could draw more interest from locals.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.205 against their IMM close at 94.185 on volume of 7,025 lots. September were at 94.005 against 93.985 on 4,240 lots.
